slides.0.title: The legal framework
slides.0.subtitle: From the mother law of 1903 to the INAVI reform of 2009
slides.1.title: Three laws
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Law 2.856 of 1903
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The mother law, giving the state control and inspection of wine. Law 18.462 rewrote its article 11: INAVI may test both domestic and imported wine products
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Law 15.903 of 1987
slides.1.highlights.1.content: From article 141 it creates INAVI; article 149 creates the wine promotion and control levy that funds it
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Law 18.462 of 2009
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Promulgated on 8 January, it rewrote INAVI's articles in Law 15.903 and listed INAVI's specific powers in article 15
slides.1.content: To read Uruguayan wine law, first tell the mother law, the founding law and the reform law apart.
slides.2.title: What INAVI can decide
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Release dates
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Article 15 of Law 18.462: INAVI may set the date when each vintage of domestic wine may be sold and moved
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Yield limits
slides.2.highlights.1.content: INAVI may set the maximum grape yield per variety and hectare
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Alcohol and additives
slides.2.highlights.2.content: It may also set the minimum alcohol for wine in circulation and the oenological products allowed for corrections. The same article adjusts the levy to the consumer price index every January and July
slides.2.content: These powers make INAVI both regulator and promoter.
slides.3.title: Who governs
slides.3.highlights.0.title: The board
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Since 2009 a Directorio has run INAVI. The transitional provisions had ministries name government delegates and asked sector groups to propose private members
slides.3.highlights.1.title: The advisory council
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Honorary. Its members come from producer and grower groups, the oenologists' association, the University of the Republic, INIA, the General Directorate of Farms and the Uruguayan School of Oenology. It meets the board at least twice a year
slides.3.highlights.2.title: The isotope database
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Article 12 of Law 18.462: the isotope-ratio database belongs to INAVI alone, and a disputed result can be re-tested at the interested party's cost
slides.3.content: Government and industry govern together, a hallmark of the Uruguayan system.
